item: Bad-item signals: paywall walls in 9 more languages, no word-count signals for zh/ja/th, 404 as a number, bare query slugs are article addresses (row 65)
summary: The 8-instance field test measured the source-quality pre-label and found: paywall phrases English-only (Amedia's 'Allerede abonnent' on 56 sources, Finnish 'Vain tilaajille' on 20); 34-46 very_short false positives per instance on complete Chinese and Japanese articles; and 24haubenin.info's 899 real articles at /?Slug URLs read as the homepage (listing_url_rate 1.0). Now: wall phrases in no/da, sv, fi, de, fr, es, it, pt and nl; the two word-count signals (very_short, high_link_density) are not assessed for an unsegmented language, in the label and in the cheap_signal selector alike, as its four metrics already were not; '404' must stand as a number; WordPress's untouched default post ('this is your first post', 4 sites) is a wall; and a query string that is one bare slug (no '=' or '&', at least 12 characters, three hyphens, not starting with a tracking or view word such as utm or amp) vetoes the homepage and section rules like an item id does. The veto only narrows what is called a non-article, so ingest drops and quarantine stamps can only fall; marks stamped before stay as they are. No re-extraction, no engine bump.
